audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] reads Pantheon while the late paragraph opens 'This is all Yasuo' and whys[6] says he 'reclaims the duel'.
audit.why: The entry's own two-item text is unambiguous and the packet's levelChart for this pairing gives Yasuo that row. Pantheon's overall 56.65% comes from the early game, not from the two-item stage.
audit.corrected: content win[6] moved from Pantheon to Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall is discussed four times with no cooldown, and Last Breath none either.
audit.why: Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s at 400 range and Last Breath 70/50/30s. Twenty-five seconds at rank 1 is a long punish window and it is the number the entire 'bait the wall' plan needs.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall's 25s written into early, mid, spikes[2], wants.you[1], breakdown.cooldowns and report[5]; Last Breath's 70s into whys[4] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'his R off your knockup-less kit ends fights' implies Yasuo needs someone else to provide the airborne target, so a Pantheon with no knock-up is safe from Last Breath in a 1v1. He is not.
audit.why: Steel Tempest's third cast is a knock-up in Yasuo's own kit. He sets up his own ultimate without any help, which means the level-6 threat in a straight 1v1 is real and the entry effectively tells the player it is not. This is the same class of omission as the calibration note about Azir vs Yasuo.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[6], spikes[3] and late: he makes his own knock-up with a third Steel Tempest.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'don't throw a long-aimed Q into an obvious Windwall window; tap Q in melee' is right but never says why, and elsewhere it is just 'your aimed Q'.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks projectiles. Comet Spear has two cast forms — Riot's own text is 'Pantheon either thrusts his spear or throws his spear' — and only the thrown form is a projectile. Saying that plainly turns a rule of thumb into a mechanic the player can reason from.
audit.corrected: Written into early, wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], late and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing says the third Steel Tempest cancels Aegis Assault.
audit.why: That cast knocks up, and Aegis Assault is a channel. Since Yasuo stacks the Q naturally through a trade, holding the shield to the end of a long exchange is the worst possible timing for it.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[2], spikes[1] and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright' — and here it is doubly confusing, because Yasuo genuinely does have a passive shield (Way of the Wanderer).
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will. On this page the phantom line reads as if it might be describing Yasuo's Flow shield winning level 1 for him, which is the opposite of what the stage says.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are your whole lane — you are one of the strongest level-1s in the game and Yasuo is a weak, squishy early laner with no flow shield built yet. The second he walks up to last-hit, W-stun onto him, tap Q for the empowered burst, and E-block his return autos; he cannot out-trade your point-and-click damage this early. Watch his W Windwall — don't throw a long-aimed Q into an obvious Windwall window; tap Q in melee or bait the wall first, then commit. His E-dash needs a minion or you to dash to, so fight him off his wave to remove the escape.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are your whole lane — you are one of the strongest level-1s in the game and Yasuo is a weak, squishy early laner with no Flow shield built yet. The second he walks up to last-hit, W-stun onto him, tap Comet Spear for the empowered burst, and face Aegis Assault at his return autos; he cannot out-trade your point-and-click damage this early. Wind Wall is 25 seconds at rank 1 and it stops projectiles — your thrown Comet Spear is one, the melee thrust is not, so tap Q up close or bait the wall first. Sweeping Blade needs a unit to dash to, so fight him off his wave.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 you stay firmly ahead — empowered-Q poke and your E directional block let you whittle him while shrugging off his early autos, and his flow shield can't absorb a full W-Q-E yet. edits.before: This is all Yasuo. notes: The most important correction is a false reassurance. The entry says 'his R off your knockup-less kit ends fights', which implies Last Breath needs an ally to launch you and that a Pantheon with no knock-up is safe from it one-on-one. Yasuo's third Steel Tempest is a knock-up in his own kit — he sets up his own ultimate unaided, so the 1v1 threat at 6 is entirely real. The same cast also cancels Aegis Assault, and because he stacks the Q naturally over a trade, the end of a long exchange is exactly the wrong moment to be channelling. On Wind Wall: the page's advice to tap Q in melee was right, and I gave it the mechanism (Riot's Comet Spear text describes a thrust and a throw; only the throw is a projectile) plus the 25-second rank-1 cooldown that the whole 'bait the wall' plan depends on. NOT ASSERTED: the kit file flags Grand Starfall as a projectile, which would imply Wind Wall can block it. That is a large claim to hang on a derived flag for a leap-and-land ultimate, and nothing in Riot's description supports it, so I wrote nothing about it. It is worth a human answer, because it decides whether Pantheon can ever ult into a Yasuo who is holding his wall. CHART: moved win[6] to Yasuo.
